title: Living Encyclopedias, Systematic Reviews, Technical Standards & Research Institutes
description: High-authority reference syntheses, formal engineering/cryptographic standards bodies, and empirical policy research institutes used to anchor esoteric concepts in established consensus.

sources.name: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (SEP)
sources.governance_and_funding: Metaphysics Research Lab at Stanford University; endowed by university libraries worldwide and public humanities grants.
concept_use_cases: Authoritative, peer-reviewed conceptual definitions of sovereignty, deterrence, Bayesian inference, causal reasoning, constitutionalism, war ethics, and scientific realism
known_limitations_and_biases: Conceptual/theoretical focus rather than empirical current-data tracking
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Cite specific SEP archive editions when defining foundational theoretical concepts, and pair with empirical domain data.

sources.name: Cochrane Library of Systematic Reviews
sources.governance_and_funding: Independent non-profit global network (Cochrane Collaboration) barring commercial pharmaceutical/device industry sponsorship of reviews.
concept_use_cases: Gold-standard meta-analytic synthesis of medical interventions, diagnostic accuracy, and public-health measures using GRADE certainty ratings
Plain-language summaries explicitly quantifying confidence intervals, risk of bias in underlying trials, and heterogeneity
known_limitations_and_biases: Strict focus on Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) can yield 'insufficient RCT evidence' findings for population-level or mechanistic interventions where RCTs are logistically difficult—distinguish 'absence of high-grade RCT proof' from 'proven ineffective'
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Always report Cochrane's GRADE certainty level (High, Moderate, Low, Very Low) alongside effect sizes, never headlines alone.

sources.name: Our World in Data (OWID)
sources.governance_and_funding: Collaboration between University of Oxford researchers and Global Change Data Lab (UK non-profit); fully open-source code and data pipelines on GitHub.
concept_use_cases: Contextualizing daily news shocks against multi-decade structural baselines (e.g., LCOE solar/battery learning curves, fertility transitions, global poverty thresholds, consumption- vs. production-based CO2 accounting)
known_limitations_and_biases: Secondary harmonizer of UN, World Bank, IEA, and academic datasets—underlying country-level measurement gaps propagate into harmonized series
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Inspect OWID's 'Sources and Processing' tab to cite both OWID and the original upstream statistical producer.

sources.name: IPCC Assessment & Special Reports
sources.governance_and_funding: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (WMO & UNEP); thousands of volunteer scientists synthesize tens of thousands of peer-reviewed papers through multi-round open expert review.
concept_use_cases: Explaining radiative forcing, equilibrium climate sensitivity, SSP emissions scenarios, tipping-point thresholds, and calibrated scientific confidence/likelihood language
known_limitations_and_biases: Multi-year assessment cycles mean literature cutoffs lag the newest 1–3 years of observations; Summary for Policymakers (SPM) undergoes line-by-line government approval, whereas underlying Working Group Technical Chapters are purely scientist-authored
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Prefer citing the underlying Working Group Technical Chapters with exact IPCC calibrated uncertainty tags (e.g., 'very likely', 'medium confidence'), supplemented by recent peer-reviewed updates.

sources.name: NIST Technical Publications, IETF RFCs & IEEE Standards
sources.governance_and_funding: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, Internet Engineering Task Force (open rough-consensus engineering body), and Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers.
concept_use_cases: Explaining exact technical mechanisms behind current-event outages or vulnerabilities (e.g., BGP route hijacking, TLS certificate revocation, post-quantum lattice cryptography, grid frequency inertia)
known_limitations_and_biases: Protocol specifications define normative behavior ('how systems SHOULD behave'), which often diverges from legacy real-world enterprise deployments
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Cite exact RFC numbers or NIST Special Publication (SP/FIPS) identifiers, and distinguish protocol design flaws from operator misconfigurations.

sources.name: Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Research
disciplines: Repo, FX Swaps & Non-Bank Financial Intermediation (NBFI)
Basel III Banking Supervision & Sovereign Risk
sources.governance_and_funding: Owned by 63 member central banks worldwide ('the central banks' bank'), headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.
concept_use_cases: Explaining esoteric financial-plumbing crises that generalist media oversimplify: FX swap basis blowouts, repo liquidity spirals, duration mismatch, shadow banking leverage, and cross-border capital flows
known_limitations_and_biases: Central-bank macroprudential orthodoxy focusing on financial stability and inflation anchoring
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Use BIS Quarterly Reviews and Working Papers to explain balance-sheet mechanics, paired with academic NBER/RePEc critiques.

sources.name: SIPRI (Stockholm International Peace Research Institute) & IISS
sources.governance_and_funding: SIPRI is an independent international institute established by the Swedish Parliament with core public grant funding; IISS (https://www.iiss.org) is a UK-headquartered international security research institute.
concept_use_cases: Providing standardized Trend-Indicator Values (TIV) for global arms transfers, nuclear warhead inventories, defense-industrial capacity, and military expenditure shares of GDP
known_limitations_and_biases: SIPRI Arms Transfers TIV measures volume of military capability transferred, NOT financial contract price—media frequently misquote TIV as dollar sales; IISS receives conference/corporate/government funding disclosed in annual accounts
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Never conflate SIPRI TIV capability units with nominal market dollars; cross-check active combat attrition against open-source visual loss trackers.

sources.name: Chatham House, Carnegie Endowment & Council on Foreign Relations
sources.governance_and_funding: Independent non-partisan policy research institutes: Royal Institute of International Affairs / Chatham House (UK), Carnegie Endowment for International Peace (global centers, https://carnegieendowment.org), and CFR (US, https://www.cfr.org).
concept_use_cases: Structured backgrounders explaining treaty architectures, alliance commitments, historical border disputes, sanctions regimes, and regional political-economy dynamics
known_limitations_and_biases: Think-tank briefs are NOT double-blind peer-reviewed academic journal articles, and largely reflect Western/trans-Atlantic policy ecosystems alongside donor/corporate membership funding
sources.citation_and_hygiene_rules: Use think-tank backgrounders for institutional synthesis, always disclose the institute's vantage point, and pair with peer-reviewed area-studies scholarship (via OpenAlex/DOAJ) and regional voices.
